title: Zinc and Its Coordination Complexes in Biological Systems
summary: This cluster revolves around zinc (Zn) and its coordination complexes, highlighting their presence in various biological systems. Escherichia coli (E. coli) contains Zn and has the gene or protein ZRT1, which inactivates zinc. Zinc is also found in cells, which contain mitochondria and vacuoles. The chemical Zn-citrate is present in E. coli, breast milk, coconut water, and yeast cytosol, while Zn-GSH is found in E. coli, coconut water, and yeast cytosol. The methods or tools CYT10 and FTS10 have peaks for Zn14.7 and Zn21.2, respectively. The chemical Zn coordination complexes are part of Zn14.7 and Zn21.2.
